blocks.text: Input action definition - discrete action trigger Actions fire when keys/buttons are pressed. They can carry optional payloads when triggered via sendAction(name, payload) from UI code. Reading it in onInput: input.pressed.<name> (went down this tick, a jump), input.held.<name> (down this tick,…

InputActionDef = { keys?: string[] // Keyboard keys that trigger this action. Key names are case-insensitive. Any KeyboardEvent.code the browser can deliver binds, spelled as the platform spells it (the UI Events code list): KeyA-KeyZ, Digit0-Digit9 (the number row), Numpad0-Numpad9 and the pad's NumpadAdd/Subtract/Multiply/Divide/Enter/Decimal/Equal/Comma, ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right, F1-F24, CapsLock/NumLock/ScrollLock, Pause, PrintScreen, ContextMenu, Insert/Delete/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown, IntlBackslash/IntlRo/IntlYen, ShiftLeft/Right, ControlLeft/Right, AltLeft/Right, MetaLeft/Right, the media keys (MediaPlayPause, AudioVolumeUp, …). Shortcut names too: a letter ("e"), a digit ("1"), space, shift, ctrl/control, alt, meta/cmd, enter, escape/esc, backspace, delete, insert, home, end, pageup, pagedown, up/down/left/right, f1-f24, numlock, and a punctuation character itself ("`", "-", "=", "[", "]", "\\", ";", "'", ",", ".", "/"). Tab is reserved by Spawn and never binds. Examples: ["space"], ["1"], ["e", "Enter"], ["escape"] mouse?: string // Mouse input that triggers this action. - "left" / "right" / "middle": mouse buttons. - "mouse4" / "mouse5": the side/thumb buttons (back/forward). Binding one suppresses the browser's history navigation for it, so quick-melee / ping / MMO binds are safe. - "wheelUp" / "wheelDown": ONE pulse per discrete wheel notch (Minecraft-style hotbar stepping). The engine quantizes raw scroll into clean ±1 detents, so a trackpad's momentum and a mouse's notches both fire exactly one step per physical detent. gamepad?: string | false // Gamepad button that triggers this action. Natural names: "a"/"b"/"x"/"y" (or "cross"/"circle"/"square"/"triangle"), "lb"/"rb", "lt"/"rt", "start"/"select", "l3"/"r3", "dpadUp"/"dpadDown"/"dpadLeft"/"dpadRight". Raw indices work too ("Gamepad:Button17" or 17). An action with keys, a mouse button or a touch chip that names no gamepad button takes the next free one of "a", "b", "x", "y", "lb", "rb", in declaration order; a button an action names is never given to another, so a button ui.js reads itself stays free only while an action names it. An action written false takes none, and its button goes to the next. A stick drives axes only, so movement a script reads key by key gets moveX/moveZ axes on those keys, read by the script instead. modifiers?: string[] // Required modifier inputs: all must be held for the action to fire. Accepts OS modifiers ("shift", "ctrl", "alt", "meta"), mouse buttons ("left", "right", "middle", "mouse4", "mouse5", same names as the `mouse` field), and key names ("space", "e", same names as the `keys` field). Combo modifiers are purely additive: they never block individual actions from firing. OS modifier strict-checking (ctrl/alt/meta block plain bindings) is preserved only for shift/ctrl/alt/meta. Examples: - ["ctrl"]: Ctrl+key (OS modifier, unchanged) - ["ctrl", "shift"]: Ctrl+Shift+key - ["right"]: primary trigger + right mouse held - ["left"]: primary trigger + left mouse held - ["space"]: primary trigger + space held activeOn?: "keydown" | "hold" | "keyup" | (string & {}) // Compat; shapes the older input.actions.<name> boolean only: "keydown" (default) = pressed, "hold" = held, "keyup" = released. held / pressed / released read every binding without it. touch?: InputActionTouchDef // Touch options. Buttons are auto-projected from keys/mouse bindings: set this to exclude an action, rename its button, pin its slot, or bind the action to a world gesture (touch: { gesture: "tap" | "double-tap" | "hold" }) for tap-the-world control schemes. active?: ScriptRef // Per-player script ref: its default export (ctx) => boolean is asked for each player at UI cadence, ctx read-only with ctx.self the player. A falsy answer takes the action from that player: none of its keys, mouse, pad buttons or touch chips bind, and their keys page does not list it. A throw keeps the last answer. }
